settings.note.logs: Run logs are saved per day in the local log folder; files older than the retention period are removed automatically
settings.note.proxy: Proxy applies to all RCON connections
settings.mcp.enable: Enable MCP server for AI clients
settings.mcp.block_mode.desc.prefix: Blocks a command that starts with the entry: stop also blocks 'stop server' and 'stopwatch'.
settings.mcp.block_mode.desc.contains: Blocks a command containing the entry anywhere: stop also blocks 'backup stop'.
settings.mcp.block_mode.desc.exact: Blocks only when the first word equals the entry: ban leaves banplayer alone, stop leaves stopwatch alone.
settings.mcp.forbidden.placeholder: Add a command, e.g. stop, ban*, Shutdown
settings.mcp.forbidden.exists: That entry is already on the list
settings.mcp.forbidden.empty: With an empty list the AI can run any RCON command — add the ones you never want it to touch.
settings.mcp.forbidden.hint: Each entry carries its own match mode; change it anytime with the dropdown beside that entry. An entry containing * is globbed against the whole command (ban* blocks ban, banplayer and 'BanPlayer 123') and ignores the match mode. This only limits MCP — commands you type in the console are unrestricted.
settings.note.mcp: AI clients start this program's MCP entry over stdio. Server addresses and passwords stay encrypted on this machine and are never sent to the model. While the switch is off the MCP process refuses to start. A command that matches the forbidden list is refused, everything else runs. Every command run and every refusal is recorded in mcp_audit.log. The forbidden list and the server list are picked up by a running MCP session without reconnecting.
